messages:
Jordan: heads-up — I started a short canary to exercise preclaim/reshuffle path after the rebalancer change. want to catch any safety gaps quickly
Priya: nice, what workload shape are you using?
Jordan: mixed: a few hot prefixes + lots of small tenants. stressing handoff + eviction.
Sam: re: safety — we need to ensure preclaim doesn't leave two nodes thinking they own the same prefix for >1s. observed race in local sim earlier.
Len: agreed. my proposal: add monotonic preclaim ids + an epoch-fence check at apply. simple CAS on lease-epoch in the handoff path.
Priya: epoch-fence seems ok. what's the failure mode? if the CAS fails, do we backoff and retry or fall back to soft-evict?
Jordan: backoff+retry for N attempts then soft-evict fallback. but need observability to surface which branch we hit.
Sam: +1. also add a fast detection: if two preclaims overlap, the later one should abort immediately based on preclaim id compare. prevents flapping.
Len: good call. preclaim id = <origin node id>-<monotonic counter>-<timestamp>. compare lexicographically.
ops-bot: canary deployed to shard s-12 at 2024-09-02T15:31: double-checking metrics route: /metrics/kv/handshake
Priya: two practical concerns: (1) eviction credits — if we preclaim but fail to make progress, we should not consume tenant eviction quota; (2) tracing: we need a trace span across preclaim->apply->confirm.
Jordan: for (1) we reserve a lightweight preclaim token that doesn't affect eviction credits; only on successful apply we debit. for (2) I already wired spans, see snippet: ```trace-id=preclaim-ctx, span=preclaim->apply->confirm```
Sam: another edge: what if preclaim succeeds, but apply gets retried due to network partition and the old owner then continues serving until TTL expiry? need graceful takeover: serve reads but route writes through sequencer that honors latest preclaim id.
Len: that's why write path needs to check lease-epoch and preclaim id before accepting mutates. reads can be served with warning tag for staleness.
Priya: perf impact? extra epoch check on every write could be hot.
Jordan: we can cache the lease-epoch in memtable with a short TTL and invalidate on preclaim events. hits become local reads 99.9% of the time.
Sam: telemetry: emit "preclaim_conflict" counter with labels {shard, tenant, outcome}. we can alert if conflict rate spikes.
Len: also add a prometheus gauge for "ownership_pending" per shard to detect lingering preclaims > 5s.
ops-bot: metric rule created: alert if ownership_pending > 0 for 30s on >2 shards.
Priya: testing: need a smoke sim that injects network partitions and clock skew. and an integration test for eviction-credit semantics when preclaim aborts.
Jordan: I'll draft a test harness by EOD. quick POC code path shown in thread: ```python
# preclaim pseudo
preclaim_id = f"{node}-{counter}-{ts}"
if lease_epoch.compare_and_swap(expected, expected+1, preclaim_meta=preclaim_id):
    apply_preclaim(preclaim_id)
else:
    handle_conflict()
```
Sam: sounds good. minor nit: prefer CAS on a packed field (epoch|owner|preclaim_id) to avoid TOCTOU.
Len: yep pack it. also document the invariants in the ownership.md section — explicitly call out read-after-write guarantees during takeover.
Priya: ok folks, next steps: Jordan implement packed-CAS + cached-epoch optimization; Sam add telemetry and alerts; Len update docs; I'll own the integration tests. timeline: PRs up by Tue.
Jordan: ack. will send a draft PR and tag @Sam @Len @Priya. thanks. :thumbsup:
